proofs.proof_tex:
By the rate-score coordinate of Theorem \(\mathrm{uniform\mbox{-}joint\mbox{-}law}\),
\[
 R_N:=\sqrt{NT_N}(\widehat p-p)\Rightarrow R,
 \qquad R\sim\mathcal N(0,\Gamma),                               \tag{22}
\]
uniformly, and \(\widehat p-p=O_{\mathbb P}((NT_N)^{-1/2})\).  Since the exact product-law center satisfies \(\vartheta_N(p;M_N)=\theta_N\), Taylor's formula at fixed \(M_N\), Lemma \(\mathrm{exact\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}capacity\mbox{-}derivative}\), and its Hessian bound yield
\[
\begin{split}
 \sqrt{NT_N}(\widetilde\theta_N-\theta_N)
 &=\nabla_p\vartheta_N(p;M_N)^{\mathsf T}R_N+\mathcal R_N,\\
 |\mathcal R_N|
 &\leq C\sqrt{NT_N}\sqrt N\,\|\widehat p-p\|^2
 =O_{\mathbb P}(T_N^{-1/2})=o_{\mathbb P}(1).                   \tag{23}
\end{split}
\]
The fallback and clipping events have probability tending to zero uniformly by the same score law and the compact interior rate bounds.  The derivative convergence in the lemma therefore gives
\[
 \sqrt{NT_N}(\widetilde\theta_N-\theta_N)
 =A^{\mathsf T}R_N+o_{\mathbb P}(1)
 \Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma A).                \tag{24}
\]
This proves the first limit and the fixed-capacity derivative formula.  Notice that only \(T_N\to\infty\) was used in the remainder in (23); no comparison of \(T_N\) with \(N\) occurs.

Let \(S_N=\sqrt{NT_N}(\widehat\theta_N-\theta_N)\).  The joint law gives
\[
 (S_N,R_N)\Rightarrow(S,R),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(S)=V,\quad \operatorname{Cov}(R,S)=\Gamma A,
 \quad \operatorname{Var}(R)=\Gamma.                            \tag{25}
\]
Subtracting (24) from the first coordinate and using (25),
\[
 \sqrt{NT_N}(\widehat\theta_N-\widetilde\theta_N)
 \Rightarrow S-A^{\mathsf T}R,
\]
whose variance is
\[
 V+A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma A-2A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma A
 =V-A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma A=W.                                   \tag{26}
\]

The diffusion Poisson derivative obeys \(H\geq1/D\).  Therefore \(A_\nu=aH>0\), and the service-score diagonal entry \(\Gamma_{\nu\nu}=\nu/a\) shows
\[
 Q=A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma A\geq \nu aH^2>0                         \tag{27}
\]
uniformly on the compact parameter set.  The score law also gives
\[
 \widehat\gamma_N-\gamma_N
 =-\sqrt N\{a(\widehat p)-a(p)\}=O_{\mathbb P}(T_N^{-1/2}),      \tag{28}
\]
and \(|\gamma_N-\gamma|\leq N^{-1/2}\).  Continuity of the Gaussian integrals defining \(H\), \(A\), and \(\Gamma\), together with compactness, hence gives \(\widehat Q/Q\to1\) uniformly in probability.  Dividing (24) by \(\sqrt{\widehat Q}\), applying (27), and using continuity of \(\Phi\) proves
\[
 \sup_{p,|\gamma|\leq G}
 \left|\mathbb P_{p,\gamma}\{\theta_N\in I_{\mathrm{fit}}\}-(1-\alpha)\right|\longrightarrow0. \tag{29}
\]
Thus the exact product-law plug-in center, its residual statistic, and its Wald interval all have the stated limits under arbitrary joint divergence.

Put \(\delta=N^{-1/2}\) and \(g=\gamma_N\).  Since \(|g-\gamma|\leq\delta\), it suffices to work on the enlarged compact staffing window \([-G-1,G+1]\).  The derivative bound in Theorem \(\mathrm{diffusion\mbox{-}poisson}\) gives \(1/D\leq h_g'\leq1/d\).  Its Poisson equation is
\[
 qh_g''(x)=-(x-m_g)-b_g(x)h_g'(x),
 \qquad b_g(x)=-dx-\nu\min(x,g).                                \tag{30}
\]
Applying the stationary diffusion identity to \(x^2\), and using \(x\min(x,g)\geq-(G+1)|x|\), gives a compact-uniform second-moment bound and hence a uniform bound on \(|m_g|\).  Equation (30) then implies
\[
 |h_g''(x)|\leq C_1(1+|x|).                                     \tag{31}
\]
On either open side of \(g\), differentiation gives
\[
 qh_g'''(x)=-1-b_g'(x)h_g'(x)-b_g(x)h_g''(x),                   \tag{32}
\]
where \(b_g'=-D\) to the left and \(b_g'=-d\) to the right.  Thus
\[
 |h_g'''(x)|\leq C_2(1+x^2)                                    \tag{33}
\]
away from the kink.  The drift, \(h_g'\), and the right side of (30) are continuous at \(g\), so \(h_g''\) is continuous there.  Hence \(h_g''\) is locally absolutely continuous and Taylor's formula with integral remainder is valid even when the jump interval meets or crosses the kink.

At the lattice state \(x=(k-Na)/\sqrt N\), let \(B_N(x)\) and \(D_N(x)\) be the available upward and downward rates.  Direct algebra gives, including at the endpoints where the unavailable rate is zero,
\[
 \delta(B_N-D_N)=b_g(x),
 \qquad
 \frac{\delta^2}{2}(B_N+D_N)
 =q+\frac\delta2\{(\tau-\lambda)x+\nu\min(x,g)\}.                \tag{34}
\]
Taylor expansion with (31)--(33) therefore yields
\[
\begin{split}
 G_{1,N}h_g(x)
 &=b_g(x)h_g'(x)
 +\left[q+\frac\delta2\{(\tau-\lambda)x+\nu\min(x,g)\}\right]h_g''(x)
 +R_N(x),\\
 |R_N(x)|
 &\leq\frac{\delta^3}{6}\{B_N(x)+D_N(x)\}
       \sup_{|u-x|\leq\delta}|h_g'''(u)|
 \leq C_3\delta(1+x^2).                                        \tag{35}
\end{split}
\]
Here \(B_N+D_N\leq3CN\).  The additional second-derivative term in (35) is bounded by \(C_4\delta(1+x^2)\) using (31).  Subtracting \(\mathcal L_gh_g=b_gh_g'+qh_g''\) gives the pointwise bound
\[
 |(G_{1,N}-\mathcal L_g)h_g(x)|\leq C_5\delta(1+x^2).           \tag{36}
\]

An independent stationary drift calculation from (34) gives
\[
 G_{1,N}x^2
 =2xb_g(x)+2q+\delta\{(\tau-\lambda)x+\nu\min(x,g)\}
 \leq-dx^2+C_6.                                                  \tag{37}
\]
Stationarity implies \(\sup_{N,p,\gamma}\mathbb E_{\rho_{1,N}}X_{1,N}^2\leq C_6/d\).  Taking expectations in (36) proves the displayed theorem with \(K_{\mathrm{res}}=C_5(1+C_6/d)\).

This is also an analytic early-kill check.  The proof is pointwise at every lattice state, includes the two physical endpoints, and treats the kink edge by absolute continuity; the exact product law only enters through stationary expectation.  Hence every ceiling phase and every asymmetric corner of \([c,C]^3\) is controlled by the same finite constant.  In the smallest interior chain \(N=2,M_N=1\), the three states are precisely the left endpoint, kink, and right endpoint, so (34)--(36) enumerate every available jump and leave no untested transition.  Finally, stationarity and the Poisson equation give
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_{\rho_{1,N}}X_{1,N}-m_{\gamma_N}\right|
 =\left|\mathbb E_{\rho_{1,N}}
   [(G_{1,N}-\mathcal L_{\gamma_N})h_{1,N}(X_{1,N})]\right|
 \leq K_{\mathrm{res}}N^{-1/2}.                                \tag{38}
\]
Thus the scaled residual cannot have a nonvanishing order-one component at a corner or ceiling phase.

All chains are stationary by Definition \(\mathrm{model\mbox{-}class}\).  Let
\[
 f_{\ell,N}=X_{\ell,N}-\mathbb E X_{\ell,N},
 \qquad -G_{\ell,N}u_{\ell,N}=f_{\ell,N},
\]
with stationary centering.  Dynkin's identity is exact:
\[
 \int_0^{T_N} f_{\ell,N}(X_{\ell,N}(t))\,dt
 =M_{\ell,N}(T_N)-
 \{u_{\ell,N}(X_{\ell,N}(T_N))-u_{\ell,N}(X_{\ell,N}(0))\}.      \tag{39}
\]
The Lipschitz and moment bounds of Lemma \(\mathrm{finite\mbox{-}chain\mbox{-}poisson\mbox{-}controls}\) imply \(\sup\mathbb E u_{\ell,N}^2<\infty\).  Since \(T_N\to\infty\), the endpoint in (39), divided by \(\sqrt{T_N}\), is \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\).  Consequently
\[
 \sqrt{NT_N}(\widehat\theta_N-\theta_N)
 =T_N^{-1/2}\{M_{0,N}(T_N)-M_{1,N}(T_N)\}+o_{\mathbb P}(1).      \tag{40}
\]

Define the compensated marked counts
\[
 U_{\lambda,N}=C_\lambda-\lambda E_\lambda,
 \quad U_{\tau,N}=C_\tau-\tau E_\tau,
 \quad U_{\nu,N}=C_\nu-\nu E_\nu.                               \tag{41}
\]
The marked-history and generator assumptions make them pairwise orthogonal martingales, with predictable brackets \(\lambda E_\lambda\), \(\tau E_\tau\), and \(\nu E_\nu\).  The exposure concentration in the finite-chain lemma gives
\[
 \frac{(E_\lambda,E_\tau,E_\nu)}{NT_N}
 \longrightarrow(s_\lambda,s_\tau,s_\nu)
 =(2-a_0-a,a_0+a,a)                                             \tag{42}
\]
uniformly in probability.  Every component is bounded away from zero by the compact positive rate bounds.  Thus the positive fallbacks are asymptotically inactive and
\[
 \sqrt{NT_N}(\widehat p-p)_j
 =\frac{U_{j,N}/\sqrt{NT_N}}{E_j/(NT_N)}.                        \tag{43}
\]

Arm independence, predictable quadratic-variation algebra, and the energy convergence in Theorem \(\mathrm{diffusion\mbox{-}poisson}\) show that the bracket of the first coordinate in (40) converges to \(V_0+V_\gamma=V\).  Equations (41)--(43) give the score block
\[
 \operatorname{diag}\left(\frac\lambda{s_\lambda},
 \frac\tau{s_\tau},\frac\nu{s_\nu}\right)=\Gamma.                \tag{44}
\]
For the cross block, a control birth has limiting occupation coefficient \(d^{-1}\), a treatment birth has coefficient \(-h_\gamma'(X)\), control and treatment natural recoveries have coefficients \(-d^{-1}\) and \(+h_\gamma'(X)\), and a service recovery has coefficient \(+h_\gamma'(X)\).  These signs follow directly from the sign \(M_{0,N}-M_{1,N}\) in (40).  The edge-average limits in the finite-chain lemma give the un-divided cross-bracket rates
\[
\begin{split}
 c_\lambda&=\lambda\{(1-a_0)/d-(1-a)H\}=\lambda A_\lambda,\\
 c_\tau&=\tau\{-a_0/d+aH\}=\tau A_\tau,\\
 c_\nu&=\nu aH=\nu A_\nu.                                      \tag{45}
\end{split}
\]
Division by the exposure limits in (43) turns (45) into \(A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma\).  Hence the full limiting bracket is
\[
 \Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}V&A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma\\
                         \Gamma A&\Gamma\end{pmatrix}.           \tag{46}
\]

We derive the Gaussian step rather than assuming it.  Project the four-dimensional martingale in (40)--(43) along an arbitrary fixed vector \(t\).  By the Poisson-increment bound and the count normalization, its largest normalized jump is at most \(C/\sqrt{NT_N}\), hence tends to zero.  Its predictable bracket converges in probability to \(t^{\mathsf T}\Sigma t\) by (10), (42), and (44)--(45).  Expanding the conditional jump characteristic factor as
\[
 e^{iu}=1+iu-u^2/2+r(u),\qquad |r(u)|\leq |u|^3/6,              \tag{47}
\]
the sum of remainders is bounded by the largest normalized jump times a tight bracket and is \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\).  Iterated conditional expectation, with stopping at a fixed bracket level and then removal of the stop, gives
\[
 \mathbb E e^{it^{\mathsf T}Z_N}
 \longrightarrow\exp\{-t^{\mathsf T}\Sigma t/2\}.               \tag{48}
\]
The characteristic functions in (48) identify the centered multivariate Gaussian limit.

Uniformity follows by contradiction: from any failing sequence in the compact rate-staffing set, select a convergent subsequence.  The moment, gradient, gap, and bracket bounds above use constants independent of that subsequence, while the Gaussian integrals defining \(V,H,A,\Gamma\) are continuous.  Applying (39)--(48) on the subsequence contradicts failure.

Finally, (43) gives uniform consistency of \(\widehat p\), and
\[
 \widehat\gamma_N-\gamma_N=O_{\mathbb P}(T_N^{-1/2}),
 \qquad |\gamma_N-\gamma|\leq N^{-1/2}.                          \tag{49}
\]
Continuity and the compact-uniform positive lower bound on \(V\) imply \(\widehat V/V\to1\) uniformly.  Studentization and continuity of \(\Phi\) prove the coverage statement.  Every identity was prelimit on \([0,T_N]\), so no path approximation over a growing interval and no upper relation between \(T_N\) and \(N\) was used.  The final scope sentence follows from Lemma \(\mathrm{boutilier\mbox{-}anchor\mbox{-}scope}\) and explicitly avoids a class-transfer claim.

Fix \(\lambda,\tau>0\) and take the continuous extension \(\nu\downarrow0\).  Then \(D\to d\), \(q=\lambda(\tau+\nu)/D\to\lambda\tau/d=q_0\), and
\[
 -dx-\nu\min(x,\gamma)\longrightarrow-dx
\]
uniformly on compact sets.  The two pieces of \(\pi_\gamma\) coalesce into the Gaussian density \(\pi_0\).  Their quadratic exponents have a common integrable Gaussian envelope for \(\nu\) in a compact neighborhood of zero, so dominated convergence gives \(m_\gamma\to0\).  The Poisson flux formula and \(1/D\leq h_\gamma'\leq1/d\) similarly give \(h_\gamma'\to d^{-1}\) in stationary \(L^2\).  Therefore
\[
 V_\gamma=2q\int(h_\gamma')^2\pi_\gamma
 \longrightarrow 2q_0/d^2
 =\frac{2\lambda\tau}{(\lambda+\tau)^3}.                        \tag{50}
\]

Now hold \(N\) and an interior capacity fixed.  The chain is finite and irreducible, its exact flux solution is bounded, and (39) expresses the centered occupation integral as a bounded-endpoint term plus a jump martingale.  The finite-state ergodic theorem follows directly from the spectral expansion used in (10), so the normalized predictable bracket converges to the exact stationary Poisson energy.  The normalized jumps are bounded by a constant times \(T_N^{-1/2}\); applying the conditional expansion (47) gives the scalar Gaussian occupation limit as \(T_N\to\infty\).  This proves the internal fixed-system reduction.  Lemma \(\mathrm{boutilier\mbox{-}anchor\mbox{-}scope}\) records that the published anchor permits distinct arm populations and capacity, so compatibility is asserted without claiming that this subclass proof transfers upward.

added_lemmas.statement:
For each arm \(\ell\in\{0,1\}\), let \(u_{\ell,N}\) be the stationary-mean-zero solution of
\[
 -G_{\ell,N}u_{\ell,N}=x-\mathbb E_{\rho_{\ell,N}}X_{\ell,N}.
\]
Uniformly over \(p\in\mathcal P\), \(|\gamma|\leq G\), and \(N\geq N_0\), the two birth--death chains have spectral gap at least \(d\), their centered scaled stationary variables have bounded moments through order six, and
\[
 0\leq \sqrt N\{u_{\ell,N}(x+N^{-1/2})-u_{\ell,N}(x)\}\leq d^{-1}
\]
on every available upward edge.  Moreover, the stationary edge averages of these scaled differences converge uniformly to \(d^{-1}\) in the control arm and to \(H=\int h_\gamma'\pi_\gamma\) in the treatment arm.  The same assertions hold for downward edges after the natural index shift.  Finally, time averages of every bounded normalized exposure or predictable-bracket integrand used by the occupation and marked-count martingales differ from their stationary means by \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), uniformly for every joint divergence \(N,T_N\to\infty\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write the birth and death rates in either arm as \(B_k\) and \(D_k\).  The rate bounds give \(a\geq c/(3C)\) and \(1-a\geq2c/(C+2c)\), so \(a,1-a\geq\beta\).  The definition of \(N_0\) is exactly the positive solution of \(\beta N-G\sqrt N\geq1\); hence \(1\leq M_N\leq N-1\).  Positivity of the rates therefore makes both finite chains irreducible.  Their stationary laws obey detailed balance,
\[
 \rho_N(k)B_k=\rho_N(k+1)D_{k+1},
 \qquad
 \rho_N(k)=\rho_N(0)\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{B_j}{D_{j+1}}.       \tag{1}
\]
Thus each chain is reversible.

Let \(g_k=\phi(k+1)-\phi(k)\) for an eigenfunction satisfying \(-\mathcal A_N\phi=\kappa\phi\).  Subtracting the eigenvalue equations at \(k+1\) and \(k\) gives
\[
 -\kappa g_k
 =B_{k+1}(g_{k+1}-g_k)+D_k(g_{k-1}-g_k)
  -\{B_k-B_{k+1}+D_{k+1}-D_k\}g_k.                              \tag{2}
\]
At a positive maximum of a nonzero gradient, the first two terms on the right are nonpositive.  Replacing \(\phi\) by \(-\phi\) handles a negative minimum.  Now
\[
 B_k-B_{k+1}+D_{k+1}-D_k
 =\lambda+\tau+\nu\{\min(k+1,M_N)-\min(k,M_N)\}\geq d           \tag{3}
\]
in the treatment arm, while the last term involving \(\nu\) is absent in the control arm.  Hence every nonzero eigenvalue is at least \(d\), proving the asserted spectral-gap bound.

Set \(\delta=N^{-1/2}\).  In the treatment arm, with \(x=(k-Na)/\sqrt N\) and \(g=\gamma_N\), direct substitution into the rates gives the exact identities
\[
 \delta(B_k-D_k)=-dx-\nu\min(x,g),
 \qquad
 \frac{\delta^2}{2}(B_k+D_k)
 =q+\frac{\delta}{2}\{(\tau-\lambda)x+\nu\min(x,g)\}.           \tag{4}
\]
The analogous control identities have drift \(-dx\) and diffusion coefficient \(q_0\).  Applying the generator to \(x^{2r}\), for \(r=1,2,3\), and using \(x\min(x,g)\geq-(G+1)|x|\) whenever \(|g|\leq G+1\), yields, by Young's inequality and induction on \(r\), constants \(c_r,C_r>0\) depending only on \((c,C,G)\) such that
\[
 G_{\ell,N}x^{2r}\leq-c_r x^{2r}+C_r(1+x^{2r-2}).               \tag{5}
\]
Unavailable boundary jumps have zero rates, so (5) remains valid at both endpoints.  Stationarity and induction imply
\[
 \sup_{N,p,\gamma,\ell}\mathbb E_{\rho_{\ell,N}}|X_{\ell,N}|^{2r}<\infty,
 \qquad r=1,2,3.                                                 \tag{6}
\]

The monotone basic coupling started from adjacent count states keeps their distance at most one until coalescence.  Its coalescence hazard is the quantity in (3), hence is at least \(d\).  The resolvent representation
\[
 u_{\ell,N}(x)=\int_0^\infty
 \mathbb E_x\{X_{\ell,N}(t)-\mathbb E_{\rho_{\ell,N}}X_{\ell,N}\}\,dt
\]
therefore gives
\[
 0\leq u_{\ell,N}(x+\delta)-u_{\ell,N}(x)
 \leq\int_0^\infty \delta e^{-dt}\,dt=\delta/d.                  \tag{7}
\]

For completeness, the exact flux representation identifies the limit of these differences.  Put \(f_i=x_i-\mathbb E X_{\ell,N}\) and \(\Delta_i=u_{\ell,N}(x_{i+1})-u_{\ell,N}(x_i)\).  Multiplying the Poisson equation by \(\rho_N(i)\), using (1), and summing from zero through \(k\) gives
\[
 \rho_N(k)B_k\Delta_k=-\sum_{i=0}^k\rho_N(i)f_i.                \tag{8}
\]
The compact-uniform invariant-law convergence in Theorem \(\mathrm{diffusion\mbox{-}poisson}\), together with the exact product ratios in (1), sends the right side of (8) to the corresponding diffusion flux and sends \(\rho_N(k)B_k/\sqrt N\) to \(q_0\pi_0(x)\) or \(q\pi_\gamma(x)\), locally uniformly.  Hence
\[
 \sqrt N\Delta_k\longrightarrow h_0'(x)=d^{-1}
 \quad\hbox{or}\quad h_\gamma'(x)                               \tag{9}
\]
locally uniformly.  Bound (7), moment bound (6), and truncation outside a fixed compact set permit dominated convergence in stationary edge averages.  Since \(K_{0,N}/N\to a_0\), \(K_{1,N}/N\to a\), and \(\min(K_{1,N},M_N)/N\to a\) in \(L^2\), (9) proves all asserted weighted edge-average limits.

Finally, reversibility and (2)--(3) give, by expansion in the finite orthonormal eigenbasis, for every bounded stationary integrand \(r\),
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\left\{T^{-1}\int_0^T r(K(t))\,dt\right\}
 \leq \frac{2\operatorname{Var}_\rho(r)}{dT}.                   \tag{10}
\]
All normalized exposure and bracket integrands in question are uniformly bounded by (7) and the rate bounds.  Equation (10) and \(T_N\to\infty\) therefore give their uniform concentration without any upper relation between \(T_N\) and \(N\).

The product weights in Definition \(\mathrm{fitted\mbox{-}center}\) satisfy the detailed-balance ratios (1).  Irreducibility makes their normalizations the unique invariant laws.  At \(p'=p\) and \(M=M_N\), they are therefore \(\rho_{0,N}\) and \(\rho_{1,N}\), which proves \(\vartheta_N(p;M_N)=\theta_N\).

Let \(\mu_{1,N}(p';M)=\sum_k(k/N)\rho_{1,N}^{p',M}(k)\).  For fixed \(M\), let \(v_N\) be the centered solution of
\[
 -\mathcal A_{1,N}^{p',M}v_N=k/N-\mu_{1,N}(p';M).
\]
Differentiating the finite identity \(\rho_{1,N}^{p',M}\mathcal A_{1,N}^{p',M}=0\), and applying the differentiated signed measure to \(v_N\), gives for each rate coordinate \(r\)
\[
 \partial_r\mu_{1,N}(p';M)
 =\mathbb E_{\rho_{1,N}^{p',M}}
   [\{\partial_r\mathcal A_{1,N}^{p',M}\}v_N].                  \tag{13}
\]
This is ordinary differentiation of a finite sum; no interchange of an infinite limit is involved.

At \(p'=p,M=M_N\), one has \(v_N(k)=u_{1,N}(s_{1,N}(k))/\sqrt N\).  If
\[
 R_N^+(k)=N\{v_N(k+1)-v_N(k)\},
 \qquad R_N^-(k)=N\{v_N(k)-v_N(k-1)\},
\]
then (13) becomes
\[
 \begin{split}
 \partial_\lambda\mu_{1,N}&=\mathbb E[(1-K_{1,N}/N)R_N^+(K_{1,N})],\\
 \partial_\tau\mu_{1,N}&=-\mathbb E[(K_{1,N}/N)R_N^-(K_{1,N})],\\
 \partial_\nu\mu_{1,N}&=-\mathbb E[(\min\{K_{1,N},M_N\}/N)R_N^-(K_{1,N})].
 \end{split}                                                     \tag{14}
\]
The edge-average limits of Lemma \(\mathrm{finite\mbox{-}chain\mbox{-}poisson\mbox{-}controls}\) imply, uniformly,
\[
 \nabla_p\mu_{1,N}(p;M_N)
 \longrightarrow ((1-a)H,-aH,-aH)^{\mathsf T}.                 \tag{15}
\]
The control product law is binomial with mean \(Na_0\), so its normalized mean has gradient
\[
 \nabla a_0=((1-a_0)/d,-a_0/d,0)^{\mathsf T}.                   \tag{16}
\]
Subtracting (15) from (16) proves the derivative limit (11), exactly in the displayed coordinates of \(A\).

It remains to justify the uniform Taylor remainder later used with this derivative.  For either product law, write \(S_r(k)=\partial_r\log w_N(k)\).  The one-step increments in \(k\) of \(S_r\) and of \(\partial_sS_r\) are bounded uniformly on \([c/2,2C]^3\): this follows term by term from
\[
 \partial_\lambda\log w_N(k)=k/\lambda,
 \quad
 \partial_\tau\log w_{1,N}(k)
 =-\sum_{j=1}^k\frac{j}{\tau j+\nu\min(j,M)},
 \quad
 \partial_\nu\log w_{1,N}(k)
 =-\sum_{j=1}^k\frac{\min(j,M)}{\tau j+\nu\min(j,M)}.           \tag{17}
\]
The control formulas are the corresponding special cases.  For arbitrary interior \(M\), the count-scale drift \(B_k-D_k\) decreases by at least \(\lambda'+\tau'\geq c\) at each step and all jump rates are at most \(6CN\) on the enlarged rate box.  Centering at the unique sign-change point of that drift and applying the generator successively to its second, fourth, and sixth powers gives \(\mathbb E|K-\mathbb EK|^r\leq C_rN^{r/2}\) for \(r\leq6\); the odd moments follow by Hölder's inequality.  This drift calculation does not require the capacity to lie in a critical window.  Consequently every centered \(S_r(K)\) and centered \(\partial_sS_r(K)\) has its \(r\)-th moment bounded by a constant times \(N^{r/2}\).

Finite-sum differentiation gives
\[
 \partial_r\mathbb E f(K)=\operatorname{Cov}(f(K),S_r(K))
\]
and
\[
 \partial_s\partial_r\mathbb E f(K)
 =\mathbb E[(f-\mathbb Ef)(S_r-\mathbb ES_r)(S_s-\mathbb ES_s)]
  +\operatorname{Cov}(f,\partial_sS_r).                          \tag{18}
\]
Taking \(f(K)=K/N\), Hölder's inequality, the sixth-moment bounds, and (17) bound the first term in (18) by \(C\sqrt N\) and the second by \(C\).  Applying this to both arms proves (12).

added_lemmas.statement: The model in Boutilier, Jonasson, Li, and Yoeli permits distinct fixed arm populations and a separately specified service capacity, and its fixed-system occupation limit and many-system fluid limit are separate results.

added_lemmas.statement:
In the additional subregime \(T_N/N\to0\), uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fit}}\),
\[
 \sqrt{NT_N}(\overline\theta_N-\theta_N)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,Q),
 \qquad
 \mathbb P\{\theta_N\in I_{\mathrm{diff}}\}=1-\alpha+o(1).
\]
Moreover \(\overline\theta_N-\widetilde\theta_N=O_{\mathbb P}(N^{-1})\) uniformly.  Thus the diffusion fitted center is an \(O(N^{-1})\)-accurate corollary, and the available residual bound makes \(T_N/N\to0\) sufficient for its Wald limit; this restriction is not imposed on exact finite-chain fitted-center inference.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For any \(p'\in[c/2,2C]^3\) and fixed interior \(M\), put \(g'=(M-Na(p'))/\sqrt N\).  The control stationary mean is exactly \(a_0(p')\), while the treatment stationary mean is
\[
 a(p')+N^{-1/2}\mathbb E_{\rho_{1,N}^{p',M}}X_{1,N}^{p',M}.
\]
Because \(M=\lceil Na(p')+g'\sqrt N\rceil\), the centering consequence of Theorem \(\mathrm{kink\mbox{-}residual\mbox{-}bound}\), applied on the enlarged compact rate box \([c/2,2C]^3\) and staffing window \([-G-1,G+1]\), gives
\[

Write
\[
 \mu=\inf_{|\gamma|\leq G}J(p,\gamma).
\]
The objective is real valued on the nonempty feasible interval by Definition \(\mathrm{design\mbox{-}objective}\), so \(\mu\) is well defined. We first treat \(G>0\). At depth \(D_\epsilon\), every surviving bisection interval \(I\) has
\[
 \operatorname{diam}(I)=2G\,2^{-D_\epsilon}.
\]
The definition
\[
 D_\epsilon=
 \left\lceil\log_2\max\{1,8GL_J/\epsilon\}\right\rceil
\]
therefore gives
\[
 L_J\operatorname{diam}(I)
 =2GL_J2^{-D_\epsilon}
 \leq\frac{\epsilon}{4}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Likewise, from
\[
 m_\epsilon=
 \left\lceil\log_2\max\{1,8/\epsilon\}\right\rceil
\]
and the rule that a depth-\(r\) call has precision at least \(m_\epsilon+r\), the terminal calls obey
\[
 e_\epsilon:=2^{-(m_\epsilon+D_\epsilon)}
 \leq 2^{-m_\epsilon}
 \leq\frac{\epsilon}{8}.                                      \tag{2}
\]
By the supplied oracle contract, every terminal interval receipt consequently has width at most
\[
 w_\epsilon:=L_J\operatorname{diam}(I)+e_\epsilon
 \leq\frac{3\epsilon}{8},                                    \tag{3}
\]
whereas every terminal midpoint point receipt has width at most \(e_\epsilon\).

Let \(U_t\) be the incumbent upper receipt after any finite stage, and let \(U_\epsilon\) be the final incumbent. Because every point receipt contains the corresponding objective value,
\[
 U_t\geq\mu,
 \qquad U_t\geq U_\epsilon.                                  \tag{4}
\]
If an interval \(I\) contains a global minimizer \(\gamma^*\), oracle inclusion gives
\[
 \underline J(I,m)\leq J(p,\gamma^*)=\mu\leq U_t.             \tag{5}
\]
Thus the strict pruning condition \(\underline J(I,m)>U_t\) never removes an interval containing \(\gamma^*\). This proves that every global minimizer belongs to the final unpruned cover \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\), without a convexity, differentiability, uniqueness, or interior-minimizer assumption.

We next show that at least one terminal interval is active and that its receipts bracket the global infimum. If \(U_\epsilon>\mu\), then for every \(\delta\in(0,U_\epsilon-\mu)\), the definition of the infimum supplies \(\eta_\delta\in[-G,G]\) with
\[
 J(p,\eta_\delta)<\mu+\delta<U_\epsilon\leq U_t.              \tag{6}
\]
Every ancestral interval containing \(\eta_\delta\) has lower receipt at most \(J(p,\eta_\delta)\), so (6) prevents its pruning. Hence \(\eta_\delta\) belongs to an active terminal interval. If \(U_\epsilon=\mu\), an incumbent point \(u\) satisfies
\[
 \mu\leq J(p,u)\leq U_\epsilon=\mu,                           \tag{7}
\]
and the same argument shows that the terminal interval containing \(u\) is active. Thus the active family is nonempty in both cases.

Define \(L_\epsilon\) as the minimum lower receipt over active terminal intervals, as in Definition \(\mathrm{capacity\mbox{-}certificate}\). For any active terminal \(I\) and any \(\eta\in I\), oracle inclusion and (3) imply
\[
 \underline J(I,m)
 \geq J(p,\eta)-w_\epsilon
 \geq\mu-w_\epsilon.                                         \tag{8}
\]
Taking the minimum over active \(I\) yields
\[
 L_\epsilon\geq\mu-w_\epsilon.                               \tag{9}
\]
On the other hand, when \(U_\epsilon>\mu\), the active interval furnished by (6) has lower receipt at most \(J(p,\eta_\delta)<\mu+\delta\). Letting \(\delta\downarrow0\) gives \(L_\epsilon\leq\mu\). When \(U_\epsilon=\mu\), the active interval from (7) has lower receipt at most \(J(p,u)=\mu\), so again
\[
 L_\epsilon\leq\mu.                                         \tag{10}
\]

It remains to control the final incumbent. If \(U_\epsilon=\mu\), the desired upper bound is immediate. Otherwise, fix \(\delta\in(0,U_\epsilon-\mu)\), let \(I_\delta\) be the active terminal interval containing \(\eta_\delta\) from (6), and let \(u_\delta\) be its midpoint. Since the interval receipt contains both objective values, (3) gives
\[
 J(p,u_\delta)
 \leq J(p,\eta_\delta)+w_\epsilon
 <\mu+\delta+w_\epsilon.                                     \tag{11}
\]
The upper endpoint of the point receipt at \(u_\delta\) is at most \(J(p,u_\delta)+e_\epsilon\). The final incumbent is no larger than that endpoint, and hence (11) yields
\[
 U_\epsilon
 <\mu+\delta+w_\epsilon+e_\epsilon.
\]
Letting \(\delta\downarrow0\), then applying (2)--(3), gives
\[
 U_\epsilon\leq\mu+w_\epsilon+e_\epsilon
 \leq\mu+\frac{\epsilon}{2}.                                 \tag{12}
\]
Combining (9), (10), and (12),
\[
 U_\epsilon-L_\epsilon
 \leq 2w_\epsilon+e_\epsilon
 \leq\frac{7\epsilon}{8}<\epsilon.                            \tag{13}
\]
The chosen \(\gamma_\epsilon\) is the incumbent point, so its point receipt and the definition of \(\mu\) give
\[
 L_\epsilon\leq\mu
 \leq J(p,\gamma_\epsilon)\leq U_\epsilon.                   \tag{14}
\]

Suppose a box was pruned when the incumbent was \(U_t\). Its recorded lower endpoint is strictly greater than \(U_t\), which is at least the final incumbent by (4). Thus every pruned record satisfies the certificate condition \(\underline J_r>U_\epsilon\). Equations (5), (13), and (14), together with the retained oracle receipts, establish every semantic condition in Definition \(\mathrm{capacity\mbox{-}certificate}\).

The complete binary tree through depth \(D_\epsilon\) has
\[
 \sum_{d=0}^{D_\epsilon}2^d=2^{D_\epsilon+1}-1               \tag{15}
\]
nodes. The fallback therefore uses at most that many interval evaluations. With at most one interval receipt and one midpoint point receipt per node, the total number of oracle requests is at most
\[
 2\bigl(2^{D_\epsilon+1}-1\bigr)
 <2^{D_\epsilon+2}
 <3\cdot2^{D_\epsilon+1},                                    \tag{16}
\]
and every requested precision is at least \(m_\epsilon\). Pruning can only decrease these counts.

Finally, if \(G=0\), the feasible set is \(\{0\}\). Query the singleton once at precision \(m_\epsilon\), set \(\gamma_\epsilon=0\), and take its rational endpoints as \(L_\epsilon,U_\epsilon\). The point contract and (2) give
\[
 L_\epsilon\leq J(p,0)\leq U_\epsilon,
 \qquad U_\epsilon-L_\epsilonleq2^{-m_\epsilon}
 \leq\frac{\epsilon}{8}<\epsilon.
\]
This is a one-record certificate and completes the conditional certification and termination proof.
